notes: Sixth sweep (2026-10-23): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (each transcript's assistant messages name only that model), uncommitted false, head d04061d and one skill_hash. git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ shows the committed rewrite, and every transcript contains the new head-rule sentence ("A head binds what selects its clause") and the new required-keys paragraph ("is dot access written long"), so the runs read the current text. All five read SKILL.md with Read; opus-1 also read references/library-design.md and references/ex_unit.md (it ran its own ExUnit checks), the others no reference file. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all five meet it, as earlier sweeps counted extra reads. In the scratch folder all five files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests: opus-1 3 of 3, haiku-1 1 of 1, haiku-2 1 of 1, sonnet-1 3 of 3, sonnet-2 2 of 3.

Changed rules. "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" is rewritten; the sentences that decide this case are "A head binds what selects its clause: a value matched against a literal, a value a guard reads, or a key whose presence selects, because another clause catches the input that lacks it.", "A head that `mix format` wraps only to move a long guard onto its own line is fine as wrapped" and "those keys select the clause by their presence, so they belong in the head even when the guard reads none of them." "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys" gains three paragraphs (body pattern on one key is dot access written long; dot chains and get_in/1; Map.fetch/2 where absent and nil differ). No run has a body pattern on one key, a dot chain into the payload or get_in/1, so the verdicts rest on the unchanged first paragraph. Opus-1 reads required keys with case Map.get(map, key) and a nil -> {:missing_field, key} clause (lines 261-262, 277-278); 2026-10-22-b graded this shape violated in baseline-opus-1 and 2026-10-22-c in skill-opus-1, so it is violated here. The new Map.fetch/2 sentence ("When those two need different handling, `Map.fetch/2` returns `:error` for the absent key and `{:ok, nil}` for the other.") does not apply, because opus-1's ParseError @moduledoc (line 75) says a missing field is "absent or `nil`", so it wants the same handling for both. The ex_unit.md change (crash-report sentence) touches no rule in this list; no run writes tests.

Head-rule bullets in the case's What to check list, violating runs out of 5. (1) The parsing head matches the keys it requires with a clause below that catches a payload lacking them: 0 of 5 violated, 5 of 5 exercised. haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 have def parse(%{"id" => ..., "type" => ..., "created" => ..., "data" => ...}) with def parse(_payload), do: {:error, :invalid_payload} below it; opus-1 has the same pair as the private parse_event/1 (lines 199, 208) under a parse/1 guarded by is_map. Each binds keys its guard does not read (type and created in haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2; all four keys in opus-1, whose head has no guard), which this bullet now counts as clean. (2) No selecting pattern moved into a body: 0 of 5 violated, 5 of 5 exercised. Every run tells a payload with its envelope keys from one without them in its heads; no run reads a payload or data key with dot access; data fields go through Map.fetch helpers (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) or Map.get helpers with a nil branch (opus-1), each a single-clause reader that returns an error instead of raising. (3) In a function with three or more clauses, no field no pattern or guard uses bound in every head, and no head pattern spread over several lines: 0 of 5 violated, 5 of 5 exercised. Each run has a four- or five-clause type mapper (event_type/1, event_kind/1, parse_type/1) matching literals, and each but sonnet-2 a three- or four-clause data dispatcher (parse_data/2, payload/2, parse_object/2) matching a literal or a guard-read type and taking data whole. The only multi-clause head that binds a field beside its selector is opus-1's four-clause ParseError.message/1 (lines 91-105), which binds the tuple element next to the tag in three of the four clauses, not every clause, and uses it in the body, so it is clean. The wrapped heads (haiku-1 lines 94-95, haiku-2 lines 82-83, sonnet-1 lines 99-100 and 124-125, sonnet-2 lines 112-113) keep the whole pattern on the first line and move only the guard, the allowed case; opus-1 wraps no head. Unlike the 2026-10-23-check batch, opus-1's message/1 probes the field half of this bullet once; the boundary it draws (a field bound in every clause) is still not probed.

Required-keys sentences in this case: no run re-matches one key in a body, writes a dot chain or calls get_in/1, so those sentences are untested here. Optional keys: haiku-1 line 145 data["failure_reason"] and haiku-2 lines 119-120 Map.get(data, "customer_email") / Map.get(data, "failure_reason") read fields their structs leave out of @enforce_keys, so they are optional and allowed. opus-1 is the only break (see above).

Closest calls, graded to the previous standard. Comments: haiku-1 marks its three public payload structs @moduledoc false (lines 22, 36, 51); the rule reserves @moduledoc false for internal modules, but earlier grades counted only comments and doctests under this rule and never a hidden public module, so it is not counted (counted, Haiku would be violated on Comments). sonnet-2's doctest expects ~U[2024-09-22 09:33:20Z] (line 103) where 1727000000 is ~U[2024-09-22 10:13:20Z]; sonnet-2's final reply says it did not run the doctests because a permission prompt blocked it; counted as 2026-10-22-d counted sonnet-1's wrong timestamp. Naming: sonnet-1 line 103 and sonnet-2 line 116 rebind data to the parsed Payment or Refund that fills Event's data field, and opus-1 line 203 likewise; earlier grades counted this as carrying the payload's key name, so clean; haiku-1's payload (line 98) and kind, and haiku-2's object, are not counted. The with rule: every with has two to five steps and no else; opus-1's currency_field/2 (line 286) and sonnet-1's optional_amount_field/2 (line 194) call another reader in a case branch, not counted, as before. Match every expected shape: the type mappers' catch-alls in haiku-1 (line 108), haiku-2 (line 96), sonnet-1 (line 113) and sonnet-2 (line 126) also receive a non-string type ("type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123}, verified), which earlier sweeps put in checks only; opus-1 guards its catch-all with is_binary and names a non-string type {:invalid_field, "type"} (line 217). sonnet-1's parse_data/2 catch-all (line 130) receives only non-map data, since parse_type/1 returns only the three atoms the clauses above it match. Outside the list: haiku-1's if inside a case (lines 166-168) goes under Keep functions short, as before; haiku-2 moved its if into check_value/3. sonnet-2's struct literals inside {:ok, ...} (lines 143-150, 159-165) are not call arguments and are not counted, as before.

Probe of 22 payloads, run in the scratch folder against each compiled file. In all five: an unknown type gives an unsupported-event error; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, not unsupported; a string or negative amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field; a non-integer or out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; a payload missing id or data gives :invalid_payload. Differences: a nil amount or nil payment_id is missing in opus-1 and invalid in the others; a missing customer_email is rejected by haiku-1 and sonnet-2 and accepted by the others; refunds carry no amount in haiku-1 and haiku-2, an optional one in sonnet-1, and a required one in opus-1 and sonnet-2; a non-string id gives {:invalid_field, "id"} in opus-1 and :invalid_payload in the others; non-map data gives {:invalid_field, "data"} in opus-1 and sonnet-1 and :invalid_payload in the others; a non-map payload raises FunctionClauseError in opus-1 (parse/1 is guarded by is_map and specced map()) and gives :invalid_payload in the others.

Compared with the previous skill sweep (2026-10-22-d at ba24972): Read required keys moves from Opus clean to violated (opus-1's Map.get readers, a shape 2026-10-22-c's skill-opus-1 also wrote); Match every expected shape moves from Sonnet violated to clean (no payment catch-all); the multi-clause rule moves from Haiku violated to clean, because the shape the previous haiku-2 was graded on (envelope keys bound in the parse/1 head) is clean under the new text and appears in all five runs here; the struct rule moves from Opus violated to clean (ParseError now has @enforce_keys); Comments stays Sonnet violated (a wrong doctest timestamp again, now in sonnet-2). Atoms, the with rule, the return-tuple rule and Naming stay clean in every tier.
